canonical_source.behavior: When Href is nonblank, AppButton renders an anchor whose effective href is the supplied Href unless Disabled; it preserves Target, Title, accessible labeling, aria-busy and aria-pressed, removes disabled links from tab order, renders busy/icon/content state, and does not wire the button OnClick callback into the link branch.

laravel_adaptation.runtime_consumer: none required for the shared component contract
laravel_adaptation.behavior: The production React AppButton selects the anchor branch only for a nonblank href, preserves href/target/title/aria state and visible content, removes href and forces tabIndex=-1 when disabled, ignores the button onClick callback in the link branch, and retains a consumer-specific canonicalOperationId separately from the shared link component identity. Whitespace href falls through to the already-terminal native button branch.

authorization.reason: This shared navigation control grants no permission and invokes no backend operation; route authorization remains owned by the destination surface.

tenant_isolation.proof: The shared component accepts no tenant/resource identifier and performs no lookup or persistence. It renders only the caller-supplied navigation target, matching the canonical component contract.

degraded_and_retry_semantics.disabled: Disabled=true removes the effective href, sets aria-disabled=true, and removes the anchor from sequential keyboard navigation with tabIndex=-1.
degraded_and_retry_semantics.busy: aria-busy and spinner state are exposed without inventing completion or success.
degraded_and_retry_semantics.retry: No internal retry is performed; navigation/runtime retry semantics belong to the destination surface.

acceptance_tests.coverage: exact canonical marker, nonblank anchor branch, href/target/title, disabled EffectiveHref removal and tab exclusion, no link-branch OnClick dispatch, busy/pressed accessibility, whitespace-Href fallback, and consumer-versus-component identity separation
regression guard proving the already-terminal non-link click branch remains a native button with its existing canonical identity and interaction semantics

terminality.basis: Source-equivalent AppButton link behavior is implemented in the production React shared component and covered by deterministic focused acceptance, including fail-closed disabled navigation; no backend authority, tenant, persistence, or provider semantics are introduced.
